stories.title: Bitcoin Core’s November 10 security disclosures: read the affected versions
stories.summary: Bitcoin Core disclosed three previously fixed issues: compact-block witness malleation could stall processing; non-default IP-whitelist configuration could wrongly privilege inbound Tor peers; TRUC sibling eviction during reorg could halt block-template creation. Two are medium severity and the TRUC issue high severity.
stories.whyItMatters: Disclosed November 10, not newly exploited November 18. These are version-specific historical vulnerabilities with released fixes. Do not imply current funds theft or that every Tor user was affected. Original pages fetched successfully.

stories.classification: Dated publisher announcement · original text reviewed
stories.summary: Luxxfolio’s October 29 release describes a non-binding letter of intent with Greywick to explore cLTC liquidity and borrowing applications on Canton. Further commercial commitments require a signed agreement.
stories.whyItMatters: A proposed reserve-backed representation is not native LTC. This announcement does not establish launch, redemption availability, DTCC acceptance or realized institutional demand.
